# Getting started

## Requirements

The publication-parity build is declared for **macOS** because the published
PDFs were produced with the Quartz device. It requires R ≥ 4.1 and twelve CRAN
packages: `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `ggplot2`, `scales`, `patchwork`, `tibble`,
`ragg`, `yaml`, `digest`, `jsonlite`, and **`mokken`**.

`mokken` is **required**, not optional — unlike in the companion Paper A
package. The application data `SWMDK` is distributed inside it and no responses
ship here.

Four command-line tools: `pdfinfo`, `pdftoppm` (figure parity), `python3`
(the disclosure scan), and `quarto` (the release-gated guide render).
`bayesmokken` is optional.

## Check the contract first

```bash
Rscript 00_setup.R
```

Reports what is missing and **installs nothing**. It reads the contract from
`config.yml`, exercises a JSON receipt parse and a one-page Quartz PDF, and
checks Quarto, so the declared and executed environment paths cannot drift.

## Rebuild everything

```bash
Rscript exhibits/00_build_all.R
```

About five seconds: 7 figures (PDF + PNG), 8 LaTeX floats, and the 144-key
ledger.

::: {.callout-important}
## Build order matters here for two reasons

`01_build_key_numbers.R` runs first because it writes the ledger every other
generator asserts against — and because it **also** derives
`outputs/derived_p16_allcell_summary.csv` from the 86,400 raw Phase 16
replication rows, cross-checking it against the locked regular-cell artifact at
a 1e-12 tolerance. Both `07_tables.R` and `08_osm_figures.R` read that file.

The driver enforces the order. Running the generators by hand out of order
fails outright rather than silently.
:::

## Check it reproduced

```bash
Rscript verification/verify_reproduction.R
#> 16 / 16 exhibits reproduce
```

The target is the **published manuscript build**, not this package's output.

## Run everything from a bare copy

```bash
bash verification/cold_start_rehearsal.sh
```

Copies the package to a temporary location, deletes the build outputs, and runs
the whole workflow **by absolute path from outside the copy**, under a directory
whose name contains a space. Both details are deliberate: they catch path
handling that only works when the working directory happens to be right, and R's
habit of encoding spaces in `--file=` as `~+~`.

## When it is not green

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `SWMDK digest does not match the Phase 17 lock` | Your `mokken` ships different data from the one the application ran on. A finding about the data source — see [the data chapter](03-data.qmd). |
| `contract violation: … expected N rows` | A frozen tier was copied incompletely. That assertion working. |
| A figure fails, geometry matches, pixels differ | Almost certainly a different Poppler build. |
| A float differs | LaTeX has no rendering tolerance; something real changed. |
| An oracle fails | A finding about the **method**, not the packaging. |

## Running the pieces individually

```bash
Rscript verification/verify_manuscript_numbers.R   # ledger digest + 69 predicates
Rscript verification/verify_semantics.R            # registers, claims, the defect check
Rscript verification/verify_governance.R           # the receipt chain
python3 verification/disclosure_scan.py            # includes the A/B severance check
Rscript verification/oracles/run_oracles.R         # LP vs two-pointer; Koopman (2022)
bash    verification/negative_controls.sh          # do the gates fail when they should
```
